papers.title: Kidzoi Enables Cell-Type-Specific Regulatory Activity and Variant Effect Prediction in Kidney.
papers.abstract: Sequence-to-function (S2F) deep learning models predict genome-wide functional profiles directly from DNA sequences and have significantly advanced our understanding of gene regulation. However, existing S2F models are fundamentally constrained by their initial training datasets, and no single model encompasses the full spectrum of cell types, clinical conditions, and cellular states, while training new models de novo is nontrivial. Here, we develop Kidzoi, a kidney cell-type-specific S2F model obtained by transfer learning from the pretrained model Borzoi using single-nucleus chromatin access
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: Kidzoi is a kidney cell-type-specific sequence-to-function deep learning model created by transfer learning from the pretrained Borzoi model using single-nucleus chromatin accessibility data. It enables prediction of regulatory activity and variant effects in a kidney-specific, cell-type-resolved manner, addressing the limitation that existing S2F models are constrained by their original training datasets. This provides a practical route to adapt general genomic models to specialized tissues without training from scratch.

papers.title: Integration of single-cell and bulk transcriptomics for deciphering prognostic value and immunotherapeutic features of floatptosis-mediated cell death in lung adenocarcinoma.
papers.abstract: Recent research has uncovered an unprecedented cell death pathway induced by outer membrane vesicles derived from Bergeyella cardium variant (BCV). This process promotes the pathological fusion of lysosome-related organelles via the SLC9A9 protein, leading to the formation of large vacuoles and ultimately inducing a terminal vacuolar cell death termed floatptosis. However, the role of floatptosis-related genes (FRGs) in lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) remains largely unexplored. In this study, we constructed a LUAD prognostic model based on FRGs to predict patient prognosis and further explored the
papers.summary: This study builds a prognostic model for lung adenocarcinoma based on genes related to floatptosis, a newly described vacuolar cell death pathway triggered by outer membrane vesicles from a Bergeyella cardium variant. By integrating single-cell and bulk transcriptomic data, the authors link floatptosis-related gene expression to patient survival and immunotherapeutic features. The work is exploratory, translating a novel cell-death mechanism into a candidate clinical biomarker framework.

papers.title: Multi-omics and pathological landscape of a senescence-associated prognostic model in bladder urothelial carcinoma.
papers.abstract: Cellular senescence contributes to tumor progression and shapes the tumor microenvironment (TME), yet its prognostic and biological significance in bladder urothelial carcinoma (BLCA) remains incompletely understood. This study aimed to identify senescence-associated prognostic signals through pan-cancer screening and to develop an integrated risk stratification framework for BLCA that bridges molecular characterization with translational relevance.
papers.summary: This study identifies cellular senescence-associated gene signatures through pan-cancer screening and uses them to build a prognostic risk model for bladder urothelial carcinoma. The model integrates multi-omics and pathological data to stratify patients and characterize links between senescence, tumor microenvironment, and clinical outcomes. It offers a translational framework for risk stratification in BLCA.

papers.title: PoolParty: streamlined design of DNA sequence libraries in Python.
papers.abstract: Computationally designed DNA sequence libraries are essential components of massively parallel reporter assays (MPRAs), deep mutational scanning (DMS) experiments, and other multiplex assays of variant effect (MAVEs). They are also increasingly used in silico to analyze genomic AI models. Designing these libraries, however, remains tedious and error-prone due to the scarcity of purpose-built software.
papers.summary: PoolParty is a Python package that streamlines the design of DNA sequence libraries for massively parallel reporter assays, deep mutational scanning, and other multiplex assays of variant effect, as well as for in silico analysis of genomic AI models. It addresses the lack of purpose-built software that makes library design tedious and error-prone.

papers.title: Microbiology Galaxy Lab: a community-driven gateway for reproducible and FAIR analysis of microbiological data.
papers.abstract: The explosion of microbial omics data has outpaced the ability of many researchers to analyse it, with complex tools and limited computational resources creating barriers to discovery. To address this gap, we present the Microbiology Galaxy Lab (MGL): a free, globally accessible, community-supported platform that combines state-of-the-art analytical power with user-friendly accessibility. Supported by the Galaxy and global microbiology communities, this platform integrates over 315 tool suites and 115 curated workflows, enabling comprehensive metabarcoding, (meta)genomic, (meta)transcriptomic,
papers.summary: The authors present the Microbiology Galaxy Lab (MGL), a free, community-supported web platform that gives microbiologists access to over 315 tool suites and 115 curated workflows for reproducible, FAIR analysis of metabarcoding, metagenomic, and metatranscriptomic data. It aims to lower computational and technical barriers that prevent many researchers from analyzing the rapidly growing volume of microbial omics data.

papers.title: Verix: a toolkit for benchmarking and harmonization of complex structural variants.
papers.abstract: Complex structural variants (CSVs) represent a critical yet under-characterized class of large-scale genomic rearrangements. CSV discovery requires not only the accurate detection of individual breakpoints but also their assembly into a single, structurally resolved CSV event. However, CSV method development is currently limited by a diagnostic gap: existing SV evaluation frameworks are designed for single-interval or single-junction SVs and cannot quantify multi-breakpoint CSV reconstruction fidelity or systematically distinguish between different types of reconstruction errors, such as over-
papers.summary: Verix is a new software toolkit designed to benchmark and harmonize complex structural variants (CSVs), which are large genomic rearrangements involving multiple breakpoints. Existing evaluation frameworks only handle simple single-breakpoint variants, so Verix fills a gap by enabling systematic assessment of how well methods reconstruct multi-breakpoint CSV events and by distinguishing different types of reconstruction errors.

papers.title: MitImpact 4: a genome-wide resource for the interpretation of coding and non-coding mitochondrial DNA variants.
papers.abstract: Mitochondrial DNA variants are a frequent cause of inherited disease, yet their computational interpretation has focused almost exclusively on the 13 protein-coding genes. Variants in tRNA and rRNA genes, which carry a disproportionate share of the known pathogenic alleles, have remained a diagnostic blind spot, because their effect depends on RNA structure rather than on protein sequence and few dedicated predictors exist. MitImpact 4 removes this asymmetry. The database now covers all 49 704 single-nucleotide variants that can occur in the mitochondrial genome and reports their functional co
papers.summary: MitImpact 4 expands mitochondrial variant interpretation from the 13 protein-coding genes to the entire mitochondrial genome, covering all 49,704 possible single-nucleotide variants including tRNA and rRNA genes. It addresses the diagnostic blind spot for non-coding mitochondrial variants by providing functional annotations based on RNA structure rather than protein sequence. This makes it a comprehensive resource for interpreting both coding and non-coding mtDNA variants in inherited disease.

papers.title: Experimental benchmarking of in silico annotations at prostate cancer risk loci and hypothesis-generating cross-cancer prioritisation of ovarian risk variants.
papers.abstract: Genome-wide association studies (GWAS) have identified numerous non-coding risk variants for prostate and ovarian cancers, yet determining which are regulatorily active and which target genes they control remains challenging. We re-analysed a dinucleotide-barcode massively parallel reporter assay (DiR-seq) of 208 bi-allelic prostate cancer risk single-nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) in three prostate cancer cell lines under false-discovery-rate (FDR) control, identifying 50 regulatory SNPs at FDR < 0.10 (30 at FDR < 0.05), including 9 shared by at least two cell lines. Benchmarking standard in
papers.summary: The authors re-analyzed a massively parallel reporter assay (DiR-seq) testing 208 prostate cancer risk SNPs across three cell lines, identifying 50 regulatory SNPs at FDR < 0.10 (30 at FDR < 0.05), with 9 shared across at least two cell lines. They then benchmarked standard in silico annotation tools against these experimental results and applied the approach to prioritize ovarian cancer risk variants by cross-cancer comparison. This provides an experimental benchmark for evaluating computational regulatory variant predictions and a hypothesis-generating framework for non-coding risk variant prioritization.

papers.title: Agent_K: An Agent-Orchestrated Pipeline for Mapping Genes to Biosynthetic Pathway towards Metabolite Discovery.
papers.abstract: The identification of biosynthetic gene clusters (BGCs) and their associated metabolic pathways is central to genome-guided natural product discovery. However, existing computational tools depend on fragmented workflows for data processing, annotation, and analysis, which require substantial manual intervention and lack seamless integration across heterogeneous platforms and tools. Here, we present, Agent_K, an agent-orchestrated framework that automates the end-to-end process from bacterial whole genome sequence analysis to biosynthetic pathway mapping and metabolite discovery as candidate ge
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: Agent_K is an agent-orchestrated computational framework that automates the entire workflow from bacterial whole-genome sequence analysis to biosynthetic gene cluster identification, pathway mapping, and candidate metabolite discovery. It addresses the fragmentation of existing tools by integrating data processing, annotation, and analysis across heterogeneous platforms with minimal manual intervention. The system aims to streamline genome-guided natural product discovery.

papers.title: Reference-free isoform discovery links unannotated RNA processing to disease risk.
papers.abstract: Disease-relevant changes in RNA processing frequently evade detection because they are missing from transcript annotations. Here, we introduce Torino , a computational framework that learns patterns of RNA processing directly from population-scale RNA sequencing data by modeling how coverage varies across samples, in datasets spanning tissues, individuals and disease states. Torino adapts non-negative matrix factorization to decompose coverage into patterns that capture RNA processing events, and to quantify their usage across samples, without transcript annotations. Across seven vertebrate sp
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: Torino is a computational framework that discovers RNA processing patterns directly from population-scale RNA sequencing data without relying on existing transcript annotations. It uses non-negative matrix factorization to decompose read coverage into reusable patterns and quantify their usage across samples, tissues, and disease states. This reference-free approach reveals unannotated RNA processing events that may be linked to disease risk.

papers.title: Streamline CNV - A Handy Nextflow Pipeline for Chromosomal Copy Number Variation Analysis.
papers.abstract: Aneuploidy, characterized by imbalanced chromosomal copy number variation (CNV), occurs in both normal somatic tissues and a wide range of diseases. Low pass whole genome sequencing (LP-WGS) to detect CNVs in cells and tissues has been widely used in all biological research. Existing informatics tools for detecting CNV often require computational expertise, often posing challenges for wet-lab biologists. To address this need, we developed Streamline CNV (SLCNV) - a user-friendly and flexible copy number analysis pipeline that allows researchers to perform many copy number-related analyses step
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: SLCNV is a user-friendly Nextflow pipeline that streamlines chromosomal copy number variation analysis from low-pass whole genome sequencing data, addressing the barrier that existing CNV tools pose for wet-lab biologists. It packages multiple copy number-related analyses into a flexible, accessible workflow, reducing the computational expertise required to detect aneuploidy and other CNVs in cells and tissues.

papers.title: Aircraft and Airport Wastewater Surveillance for Public Health Preparedness Demands an Integrated and Sustainable Approach.
papers.abstract: As domestic and international travel has expanded, the risk of the cross-border dissemination of infectious pathogens has increased, as clearly evidenced during the COVID-19 pandemic. Aircraft- and airport-based wastewater surveillance can provide timely, aggregate evidence of pathogen circulation among mobile populations and may complement clinical, genomic, and syndromic surveillance at points of entry. The strongest evidence for this approach comes from SARS-CoV-2 RNA detection and variant monitoring in aircraft lavatory wastewater, airport terminal wastewater, and airport-associated wastew
papers.summary: This perspective argues that wastewater surveillance at airports and on aircraft can provide early, aggregated signals of pathogen circulation among travelers, complementing clinical and genomic surveillance at borders. The strongest evidence so far comes from detecting SARS-CoV-2 RNA and variants in lavatory and terminal wastewater. The authors call for an integrated, sustainable framework for deploying this approach for public health preparedness.

papers.title: Serial Cryosectioning for the Spatial Transcriptomics of Plant Tissues.
papers.abstract: Spatial transcriptomics enables genome-wide gene expression profiling while preserving tissue architecture, making it a powerful approach for studying plant developmental transitions. However, preparing small and structurally complex plant tissues for spatial transcriptomics remains technically challenging because samples must be rapidly preserved, precisely oriented, serially sectioned, and accurately positioned within the limited capture area of the Visium slides. Here, we describe an optimized workflow for cryo-embedding, serial cryosectioning, section placement, and data analysis of small
papers.summary: This protocol describes an optimized workflow for preparing small, structurally complex plant tissues for 10x Visium spatial transcriptomics, covering cryo-embedding, serial cryosectioning, precise section placement on capture slides, and downstream data analysis. It addresses the practical challenges of rapidly preserving, orienting, and positioning delicate plant samples within the limited capture area, making spatial transcriptomics more accessible for plant developmental studies.

papers.title: Synthetic Reconstruction and Characterization of Endogenous Bacteriophage Genomes from Desulfovibrio vulgaris.
papers.abstract: Microbiologically influenced corrosion (MIC) caused by sulfate-reducing bacteria (SRB) is a major challenge in industrial infrastructure, yet the limited availability of well-characterized bacteriophages has hindered the development of phage-based strategies for controlling these organisms. Here, we present an integrated genome-guided workflow for the discovery, validation, and synthetic reconstruction of endogenous prophages from the model sulfate-reducing bacterium Desulfovibrio vulgaris Hildenborough. Bioinformatic analysis using PHASTEST identified seven prophage-like regions distributed t
papers.summary: The authors developed a genome-guided workflow to identify, validate, and synthetically reconstruct endogenous prophages from the sulfate-reducing bacterium Desulfovibrio vulgaris Hildenborough, a model organism for microbiologically influenced corrosion. Bioinformatic analysis revealed seven prophage-like regions, and the team successfully reconstructed and characterized these phages, providing new tools for potential phage-based control of corrosive biofilms. This work expands the limited repertoire of well-characterized bacteriophages for SRB and demonstrates a generalizable pipeline for prophage discovery and synthetic revival.

papers.title: Combining MAVEs and computational predictors improves variant classification across ancestries in hereditary cancer genes.
papers.abstract: Many commonly used computational tools for variant effect prediction exhibit ancestry-related bias because they are trained on clinical or population datasets that under-represent global diversity, leading to uneven and sometimes unfair variant classification across ancestries. Multiplexed assays of variant effect (MAVEs) and population-free variant effect predictors (VEPs) instead offer alternatives that are unbiased with respect to human ancestry, providing classification evidence that generalises across populations.
papers.summary: The paper shows that commonly used computational variant effect predictors are biased by ancestry because their training data under-represent global populations. It proposes combining multiplexed assays of variant effect (MAVEs) with population-free predictors to produce variant classifications that generalize fairly across ancestries in hereditary cancer genes.

papers.title: Identification of Genes Associated with Gut Microbiota Metabolites in Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus Complicated by Acute Cerebral Infarction Based on Bioinformatics and Mendelian Randomization.
papers.abstract: Background: Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) and acute cerebral infarction (ACI) are globally prevalent diseases that impose substantial public health burdens. While gut microbiota (GM) is increasingly recognized to regulate metabolic and immune homeostasis linked to both diseases, its shared genetically predicted microbial taxa and underlying metabolite-gene regulatory mechanisms in T2DM and ACI remain unclear, highlighting the need for systematic investigation. Accordingly, this study aimed to elucidate their regulatory mechanisms. Methods: Transcriptomic datasets, genome-wide association stu
papers.summary: This study integrates transcriptomic data with Mendelian randomization to identify gut microbiota taxa and metabolites that are genetically linked to both type 2 diabetes and acute cerebral infarction, then maps these to candidate genes. The work proposes shared microbial-metabolite-gene regulatory axes that may underlie the co-occurrence of these two conditions. Findings are exploratory and require experimental validation.

papers.title: Deep Genomic Characterization of Bacillus subtilis SNUY1 & 168 Using MAYA (Multistage Analysis of Prokaryotic Annotations): An Integrated Snakemake-Based Bioinformatics Pipeline.
papers.abstract: Bacillus subtilis is an extensively characterized Gram-positive bacterium with broad applications in agriculture, biotechnology, and biocontrol. Strain SNUY1, known for its antifungal properties and use as an edible coating, has been completely sequenced and deposited in NCBI (accession: CP199918), making it an important model for genomic and functional characterization. Here, we present the MAYA pipeline, a fully automated, rule-based Snakemake workflow that integrates eighteen bioinformatic tools into a single end-to-end framework. MAYA accepts either raw Illumina paired-end FASTQ reads or p
papers.summary: The authors present MAYA, an automated Snakemake-based pipeline that integrates eighteen bioinformatics tools to perform end-to-end genomic annotation and characterization of prokaryotes from raw Illumina reads or assembled genomes. They demonstrate it by deeply characterizing Bacillus subtilis strains SNUY1 (an antifungal, edible-coating strain) and the model strain 168, providing a reproducible workflow for prokaryotic genome analysis.

papers.title: KmerSignificance score: A discriminative and biologically informed framework for viral k-mer prioritization.
papers.abstract: Distinguishing closely related viral strains requires identifying genomic regions where subtle sequence differences carry biological significance. While k-mer-based approaches offer computational efficiency for genome analysis, existing methods lack standardized frameworks for evaluating which k-mers are most informative. Current selection strategies focus primarily on statistical discriminative power without integrating biological context. We introduce KmerSignificance Score (KSS), a k-mer prioritization framework combining three components: an information-theoretic method measuring strain-di
papers.summary: The authors introduce the KmerSignificance Score (KSS), a framework for prioritizing k-mers that combines statistical discriminative power with biological context to better distinguish closely related viral strains. KSS integrates an information-theoretic measure of strain discrimination with additional biologically informed components, addressing the gap in standardized k-mer selection methods. This provides a more interpretable and biologically relevant way to choose informative k-mers for viral genome analysis.

papers.title: Integrated optimization of experimental and computational workflows improves genome recovery in long-read gut metagenomics.
papers.abstract: Short-read metagenomic sequencing has been widely applied in microbial research due to its high quality and decreasing cost. However, short reads are inherently fragmented, which limits assembly contiguity and the recovery of complete microbial genomes. In contrast, long-read sequencing, with significantly longer read lengths, helps overcome these limitations. Achieving complete and accurate genome recovery is the core goal of metagenomics. To address this challenge, we systematically evaluated and optimized the long-read metagenomic workflow, from sample processing to computational assembly,
papers.summary: This study systematically evaluates and optimizes a long-read metagenomic workflow for gut microbiome samples, spanning sample processing through computational assembly, to improve recovery of complete microbial genomes. The authors identify workflow choices that enhance assembly contiguity and genome completeness relative to standard practices. The work provides practical guidance for labs seeking to move beyond fragmented short-read assemblies toward closed genomes.

papers.title: Conservative evolution of genetic and features in Caenorhabditis becei, an experimentally tractable gonochoristic worm.
papers.abstract: Caenorhabditis nematodes represent a promising model clade for evolutionary genetics and genomics, but research has focused on the three androdioecious species, those with self-fertile hermaphrodites, all in the Elegans Group of species. The majority of Caenorhabditis species are gonochorists, with males and females, characterized by inconveniently high heterozygosity and inbreeding depression. We have identified C. becei as an experimentally tractable gonochorist. We show that transmission-genetic properties known from the androdioecious Elegans Group species are conserved in this Japonica Gr
papers.summary: The authors identify Caenorhabditis becei, a gonochoristic (male-female) nematode, as an experimentally tractable model for evolutionary genetics, addressing the field's overreliance on self-fertile hermaphroditic Elegans Group species. They show that transmission-genetic properties known from androdioecious Elegans Group species are conserved in this Japonica Group species, suggesting broader applicability of established genetic tools and principles.

papers.title: Inferring causal networks for genomic trios with high-dimensional confounding variables.
papers.abstract: Causal structure inference under the principle of Mendelian randomization (PMR) enables the study of causal relationships between two molecular phenotypes (e.g. gene expression) by leveraging genetic variants as instrumental variables to impose constraints on edge direction. In practice, inference is often affected by numerous confounding variables, such as other genes, other processes and demographic variables, making it essential to robustly account for confounders. However, existing methods have limited ability to accommodate high-dimensional confounding. Here, we introduce Mendelian random
papers.summary: The paper introduces a new method for inferring causal relationships between molecular phenotypes (like gene expression) using genetic variants as instruments under the Mendelian randomization principle, specifically designed to handle high-dimensional confounding variables such as other genes, processes, and demographic factors. Existing methods struggle with such high-dimensional confounders, and this work aims to robustly account for them in causal network inference for genomic trio data.

papers.title: SCCmecExtractor: a tool for extracting staphylococcal cassette chromosome elements from whole-genome sequences.
papers.abstract: Staphylococcal cassette chromosome (SCC) elements are mobile genetic elements that integrate at the rlmH gene and are predominantly responsible for methicillin resistance in staphylococci. Although staphylococcal cassette chromosome mec (SCCmec) typing tools exist, none can extract the element sequence itself or explicitly classify SCC elements that lack methicillin resistance genes. Here, we present SCCmecExtractor, a lightweight Python toolkit that identifies SCC element boundaries through degenerate attachment site (att) pattern matching, extracts complete elements from whole-genome assembl
papers.summary: SCCmecExtractor is a lightweight Python toolkit that identifies and extracts complete staphylococcal cassette chromosome (SCC) elements from whole-genome assemblies by matching degenerate attachment site patterns. Unlike existing SCCmec typing tools, it can extract the full element sequence and classify SCC elements even when they lack methicillin resistance genes. This fills a gap for studying the diversity and mobility of these important mobile genetic elements.

papers.title: The Promise and Limitations of Metabolic Trait Prediction Across Diverse Bacteria.
papers.abstract: Metabolic traits mediate microbial interactions and underpin mechanistic models of community assembly. With the rapid expansion of genomic data and bioinformatic tools, it is widely assumed that metabolic traits such as substrate utilization can be reliably inferred from genomes alone. Here, we systematically evaluate this assumption by comparing genome-based predictions from four commonly used tools to high-throughput growth phenotypes of 186 marine bacteria. For simple substrates, prediction accuracy was limited and highly variable across taxa and substrates, with many strains predicted at o
papers.summary: This study tests the common assumption that bacterial metabolic traits can be reliably predicted from genome sequences alone. Comparing four popular bioinformatic tools against high-throughput growth phenotypes of 186 marine bacteria, the authors find that predictions for simple substrates are limited in accuracy and vary widely across taxa and substrates, with many strains incorrectly predicted. The work highlights important limitations of genome-based metabolic inference and cautions against over-reliance on such tools.

papers.title: Long-read sequencing of FLG identifies extensive copy number variation in exon 3 and detects rare loss-of-function variants.
papers.abstract: Loss-of-function (LOF) variants of the FLG gene are risk factors for atopic dermatitis. However, owing to the repetitive nature of exon 3, these variants are difficult to characterize. We sought to determine whether the use of long-read technologies would enable better characterization of the FLG gene and improve the detection of LOF variants. We sequenced a diverse clinical cohort of 192 samples collected in Belgium, Ireland, and Rwanda using long-read sequencing as well as publicly available data. We identified both common and rare LOF variants linked to atopic dermatitis in our clinical coh
papers.journal: JID innovations : skin science from molecules to population health
papers.summary: Using long-read sequencing on 192 samples from Belgium, Ireland, and Rwanda, the authors characterized the repetitive exon 3 of FLG, revealing extensive copy number variation and identifying both common and rare loss-of-function variants associated with atopic dermatitis. Long-read technology improved detection of these variants that are difficult to resolve with short-read methods.

papers.title: Design and validation of nucleosome binding peptides using BindCraft.
papers.abstract: Chromatin is a sophisticated assembly of DNA, RNA and proteins in the nuclei of eukaryotic cells. Protein-protein interactions that govern chromatin function are key regulators of genome activity, making them prime targets for drug discovery. Engineering and modulating these contacts presents a viable pathway for innovative epigenetic therapies. Nucleosomes, the primary structural units of chromatin, feature various interaction interfaces, most notably the acidic patch. This region serves as a critical binding site for numerous chromatin-associated proteins, often via their intrinsically disor
papers.summary: The authors used the deep-learning protein design tool BindCraft to design short peptides that bind the nucleosome acidic patch, a key chromatin interaction hub, then experimentally validated the designs. This demonstrates that computational de novo design can generate chromatin-targeting peptides, opening a route toward epigenetic therapeutics that modulate nucleosome-protein contacts.

papers.title: Assembly and comparative analysis of the mitochondrial genome of Pteroceltis tatarinowii Maxim. (Cannabaceae), a tertiary relict plant endemic to China.
papers.abstract: Pteroceltis tatarinowii Maxim. (Cannabaceae) is a deciduous arbor endemic to China. As a Tertiary relict plant, it is listed as a rare and endangered species under national Class III key protection. Mitochondrial genomic data of P. tatarinowii can improve our knowledge of phylogenetic relationships within Cannabaceae, resolve the taxonomic placement and evolutionary divergence of the genus Pteroceltis, and supply molecular support for conservation and genetic breeding of this endangered tree.
papers.summary: This study assembled and analyzed the mitochondrial genome of Pteroceltis tatarinowii, a rare Tertiary relict tree endemic to China. The mitochondrial genomic data were used to clarify phylogenetic relationships within Cannabaceae and to resolve the taxonomic placement and evolutionary divergence of the genus Pteroceltis. The work provides molecular support for conservation and genetic breeding of this endangered species.

papers.title: ogMapper improves speed and memory for short-sequencing read mapping using a novel guided sparse genome index.
papers.abstract: Short DNA-read sequencing has become an everyday essential tool in research and clinical setting. Read mapping is a crucial step that consumes large amounts of memory and CPU time, limiting the hardware required and ultimately restricting its applications. The memory required for the genome index can be approximated as βG, where G is the genome size and β is a factor that depends on the implementation. For example, β ≈ 10 for bwa-mem2 or β ≈ 1.9 for minimap2. Here, an indexing strategy is presented in which β can be even less than 1, commonly around 0.5. The indexing strategy relies on "guides
papers.summary: ogMapper introduces a new genome indexing strategy for short-read mapping that reduces memory usage to roughly half the genome size (β ≈ 0.5), compared to β ≈ 10 for bwa-mem2 and β ≈ 1.9 for minimap2. The approach uses a 'guided sparse' index to lower memory and CPU requirements, making read mapping more accessible on modest hardware. This could broaden the applicability of short-read sequencing in research and clinical settings.

papers.title: pycircdb: integrated circRNA database annotation for computational workflows.
papers.abstract: Currently, multiple databases exist for the annotation of circular RNAs, providing descriptions of their genomic features, FASTA sequences, predicted microRNA targets and RNA-binding protein interactions. Despite the availability of these resources, annotation remains cumbersome. Conflicting identifiers and genomic coordinates for circular RNAs across databases pose a challenge to reproducibility for users. Furthermore, current databases primarily provide access via web-based graphical user interfaces, bulk downloads and limited programmatic access, rendering their use in computational workflo
papers.summary: pycircdb is a new Python package that integrates multiple circRNA databases into a single programmatic interface, resolving conflicting identifiers and genomic coordinates to improve reproducibility. It enables seamless access to circRNA annotations—including sequences, microRNA targets, and RNA-binding protein interactions—within computational workflows, addressing the limitations of web-based or bulk-download-only resources.

papers.title: vardictcpp: a C++ reimplementation of VarDict variant caller.
papers.abstract: Genomic variant calling is a central computational task in disease research and diagnostics, where somatic mutations such as JAK2 V617F serve as diagnostic markers in myeloid neoplasms. VarDict, originally written in Perl, and its reimplementation VarDictJava are widely used variant callers in the bioinformatics community. The Perl implementation requires run times of up to several hours; VarDictJava reduces this to a few minutes but can consume large amounts of main memory, which limits the number of jobs that can be run in parallel on a given machine. We present vardictcpp, a functionally id
papers.summary: vardictcpp is a C++ reimplementation of the widely used VarDict variant caller, which was originally written in Perl and later reimplemented in Java. It aims to address the performance limitations of the Perl version (hours-long runtimes) and the high memory consumption of VarDictJava, enabling more parallel jobs on a given machine. The tool is functionally identical to VarDict, making it a drop-in replacement for somatic variant calling.

papers.title: Integrating multi-omics with machine learning: from genomic variant functional annotation to pharmacogenomics and biomarker discovery.
papers.abstract: Integrating heterogeneous multi-omics data with machine learning (ML) provides a powerful framework for interpreting genomic variants and advancing pharmacogenomic research in precision medicine. High-throughput technologies have generated vast datasets spanning genomics, transcriptomics, epigenomics, and proteomics, yet integrating these high-dimensional data into clinically meaningful insights remains a major computational challenge. Machine learning and deep learning models, including Graph Neural Networks (GNNs), Transformers, and Variational Autoencoders (VAEs), offer promising solutions.
papers.summary: This review surveys how machine learning and deep learning models—including graph neural networks, transformers, and variational autoencoders—are being used to integrate multi-omics data for genomic variant functional annotation, pharmacogenomics, and biomarker discovery. It frames the computational challenge of combining high-dimensional genomics, transcriptomics, epigenomics, and proteomics data into clinically actionable insights for precision medicine.
